IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Perf-canary failure detected
Job: `quant-perf-nightly` (perf-canary)
Run: https://perf-canary.redwood.dev/runs/quant-perf/1730451001
Status: FAIL
Signal: p95 TPOT regression > threshold
Tags: `runtime=redwood@9f3c2b1` `gpu=H100` `model=qwen2.5-7b-instruct` `quant=INT8` `scenario=streaming_chat`
Owner ping: @Connor O'Brien @Sean Gallagher @Sahana Iyer

Sean Gallagher: seeing it too. Not customer-facing (nightly), but it’s blocking the release train gate. Anyone already looking at what changed between baseline and candidate?

Sahana Iyer: comparator says +18.7% p95 TPOT vs last green. TTFT is basically flat (+1-2%). It’s mostly decode tail.

Allison Grant: dashboard panel for this run: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/quant-perf/quant-perf?var-run=1730451001
The queue wait histogram is also shifted right for INT8 decode. (new scheduler instrumentation is helpful here)

Connor O'Brien: what’s the candidate set? is this on the release branch or main nightly?

Sahana Iyer: nightly is pinned to `runtime@9f3c2b1` (release-candidate tag from yesterday). Baseline is `runtime@7a81dce` (last green). Canary config: https://github.com/redwood/perf-canary/blob/main/jobs/quant-perf-nightly.yaml

Noah Patel: quick diff: 9f3c2b1 includes:
- PR #10624 scheduler batch-size cap override for quantized decode
- PR #10632 queue wait hist export
- PR #10623 INT8 GEMM conversion overhead reduction
(and a couple logging spans behind flags)
My guess is #10624 if it’s decode p95.

Sofia Ivanova: #10624 changes batch cap for quant decode *only* when mixed prompt lengths detected. If the canary workload is mixed (it is), it could reduce batching efficiency and shift tail.
But +18% is bigger than we expected.

Marcus Reed: can reproduce locally-ish in perf lab on H100: with the cap enabled, tokens/sec drops ~6-8% but p95 TPOT can jump depending on concurrency. If background contention exists it amplifies.

Sean Gallagher: perf lab nodes are clean right now (no other jobs). Clocks are locked and temps ok. So likely real.

Grace Kim: any chance this is the INT8 selector bug again (choosing FP16 kernel + extra conversions)? That would show up as higher per-token but also more kernel time.

Rina Kobayashi: I pulled the per-phase breakdown artifact from the canary run. Prefill time is basically unchanged, decode phase time increased and *queue_wait_decode* is higher.
Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/quant-perf/1730451001/phase_breakdown.json

Allison Grant: looking at the trace sampling we have (limited). It’s not obviously spending more time in GEMM kernels; the “waiting to be scheduled” portion increases.

Noah Patel: that points back to scheduler caps. The cap can force smaller decode batches => more scheduling overhead + less KV reuse benefits.

Connor O'Brien: decision needed: release gate is red right now. Options:
1) revert/disable #10624 for this train
2) keep but loosen threshold / allowlist (not ideal)
3) ship behind a default-off knob (if not already)
What’s the fastest safe move?

Sofia Ivanova: #10624 is behind `scheduler.quant_decode_batch_cap` with default ON in the RC config (we flipped it as part of the sprint defaults). We can flip default back to OFF for this train and still keep the code for experiments.

Sahana Iyer: from canary POV we can pin the knob OFF in the canary job config immediately, but release gate should reflect intended defaults. I’d prefer we revert the default flip.

Marissa Cole: +1. If we ship with default ON and then have to hotfix after release, it’s messy. Better to ship conservative default and continue A/B.

Sean Gallagher: agree. Since this is a regression on the canary workload, we should treat it as real until proven otherwise.

Connor O'Brien: ok. Action:
- rollback default: set `scheduler.quant_decode_batch_cap` default back to OFF in release config
- keep code path available for experiments
- rerun canary with default OFF to confirm gate green
Sahana, can you open the revert PR or config change? I’ll mark the release train as “blocked pending rerun”.

Sahana Iyer: on it. I’ll also add an allowlist note so we don’t accidentally flip it again without a canary result.

Grace Kim: while that happens I’ll sanity check INT8 kernel times vs baseline just to ensure there isn’t a separate regression masked by queue wait.

Allison Grant: I can add a dashboard annotation for this incident + the knob change so the next run is easy to compare.

IncidentBot: Update requested by @Connor O'Brien
Impact: Internal only (perf-canary gate)
Status: Mitigating
Next update: after canary rerun

Marcus Reed: fyi: if we still want some tail help, maybe cap only when concurrency > N *and* prefill queue is backlogged. Current heuristic might be too aggressive.

Sofia Ivanova: yep. We’ll follow up in the scheduler experiment matrix. For now: conservative.

Connor O'Brien: thanks all. Call is to rollback the default flip for this train. Once canary is green, we proceed.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: Please post the rerun link in-thread when it finishes.

Sahana Iyer: PR up: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/10641 (revert default for `scheduler.quant_decode_batch_cap` in RC config). Kicked canary rerun with knob OFF: https://perf-canary.redwood.dev/runs/quant-perf/1730453602

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation in progress
Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/10641

Allison Grant: rerun is already trending better on the live panel. will confirm once it finishes.

Connor O'Brien: cool. If rerun is green, we’ll close this as “internal perf regression caught by canary; mitigated by default rollback” and schedule the heuristic tuning as follow-up.
